human_tolerance.notes: Judgement based on reports of coyotes foraging in residential areas beside forest cover; availability and human pressure affect use.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Reported US breeding timing varies: generally January to March, with February to May reported in the Sierra Nevada. This is a broad evidence envelope, not a uniform local season.

vocalizations.description: Howls and yips are heard in the morning and evening; the exact calling context and rate vary by group and place.

external.note: GBIF usage key 5219153 was checked at its API record; Wikidata Q44299 contains iNaturalist taxon id 42051 and GBIF key 5219153 (properties P3151 and P846). The iNaturalist API independently returned active species rank for id 42051.

range.note: FEIS lists coyotes coast-to-coast and in every US state, and says Florida and Georgia populations were introduced. US is recorded as the country-level native range for this national activity record; US-FL and US-GA retain the documented introduced pockets.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk, trot, and gallop are represented as terrestrial modes. NPS documented an individual coyote swimming from Angel Island to Alcatraz. The shared behavior does not execute swim, and the preview swim pose does not depict it convincingly.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Endotherm is the standard mammalian classification.

traits.nest_type.note: Uses dens, including burrows made by other animals.

traits.size_class.note: Medium is a simulation size category judgment for the dataset body-mass value.

traits.mass_kg.note: MamFuncDat row 4926 reports 13,406.33 g, sourced there to Smith et al. (2003), Ref_117. Converted to kg by dividing by 1,000 and rounded to 13.4 kg. This cross-species mammal compilation value is used as a representative adult estimate; it is not a US population-specific mean.

traits.lifespan_y.note: The required field asks for typical wild lifespan. FEIS says few wild coyotes live more than 6 to 8 years but does not report a typical mean. Six years is an explicitly conservative authored proxy at the lower end of that interval, not a measured mean.

traits.diet.note: MamFuncDat row 4926 reports 60% vertebrate endotherms, 10% vertebrate fish, and 30% scavenged vertebrate food. Mapped to the schema's vertebrate, fish, and carrion shares; this is a broad compiled diet model, not a local stomach-content estimate.

traits.social.note: Group with size range 1-6 represents the observed variation from solitary individuals to groups; social organization depends on prey and season.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Cathemeral: active in daytime and nighttime, with activity peaks around sunrise and sunset and generally more nocturnal foraging.

traits.defense.note: Flee is a simulation response choice for a mobile mammal.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.6 represents an adaptable animal that generally avoids people while using some residential areas.

habitat.use.note: Judgement: ground 0.9 and fossorial 0.1 represent terrestrial foraging and den use; they are not measured time budgets.

habitat.resources.note: Resource weights mirror the normalized EltonTraits categories: 60% vertebrate endotherms and 10% fish are combined as 70% small_vertebrate prey, with 30% scavenged vertebrate food. Burrow and shrub_thicket represent reported den and cover use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Adapter and garden use are authored classifications based on reported foraging in residential areas adjacent to forest cover.

seasonal.note: Coyotes remain active year-round. The breeding window records the reported US timing envelope (generally January-March, February-May in the Sierra Nevada), not one universal local season.

activity.note: The fetched US curve uses GBIF tier A only. The iNaturalist tier C query returned zero records and was not used.

behavior.note: Shared ground-forager program uses walk to forage, gallop to flee, and rests when energy is high. The sun-rest interval is narrowed to 90-90 degrees so the animal can remain active both day and night, matching the cathemeral source summary. Only small vertebrate prey is a reachable feeding action; fish, carrion, and plant foods remain unmodeled. The FSM has no swim action; the preview swim pose is not a convincing swimming posture, and the built-in rest pose remains standing.

look.note: Judgement: proportions and fur colors are stylized model choices informed by the NPS description of the coyote form, coat color, black-tipped fur, and tail. They are not measured rendering specifications.

traits.length_m.note: NPS states nose-to-tail length may be 4 feet or more. Converted the 4-foot lower bound to 1.22 m (4 × 0.3048); this is not a mean.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Judgement: 0.52 m is the midpoint conversion of the NPS reported 18-23 inch shoulder-height range (0.457-0.584 m).

vocalizations.note: NPS reports coyotes howling and yipping in morning and evening. Zero cooldown and contact classification are simulation representation choices.
